html:
Averroes, in Arabic Ibn Rushd, was a philosopher, judge and doctor from Córdoba in al-Andalus, born in 1126. His commentaries on Aristotle made him known in Latin Europe simply as "the Commentator".

He came from a family of judges and served the Almohad caliphs as chief judge of Seville and Córdoba and as court doctor in Marrakesh. At the caliph's request he wrote commentaries on nearly all of Aristotle's works. He also wrote a medical encyclopedia and a defence of philosophy against the attacks of the theologian al-Ghazali, arguing that reason and revealed religion cannot truly conflict. Late in life he fell from favour and his books were banned for a time, before he was recalled. He died in Marrakesh in 1198.

He mattered more to Christians and Jews than in the Islamic world. Translated into Latin in the 13th century, his commentaries shaped university teaching in Paris and Italy. A movement called Latin Averroism grew around him, and Thomas Aquinas drew on his work while arguing against some of his ideas.
sum: Averroes, in Arabic Ibn Rushd, was a philosopher, judge and doctor from Córdoba in al-Andalus, born in 1126. His commentaries on Aristotle made him known in Latin Europe simply as "the Commentator".
